author: Kang Jun-young
description:
The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. The venue is not accidental. Forty years ago, this was a border town of rice fields and duck ponds; it is now where a good part of the world’s electronics are designed and built, and the showcase of China’s “reform and opening up”.
The event’s theme, “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together”, puts openness, innovation and cooperation at the centre. US President Donald Trump...
title: Amid the Xi-Trump clamour, can Apec revive the business of cooperation?

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
Disciplinary staff in Wuhan, provincial capital of Hubei in central China, were going about their routine workday when a red alert landed. It was from a large data model – flagging a possible case of corruption.
“A company took on more than 10 projects this year. Its registered capital reduced from 50 million yuan (US$7.5 million) to 10 million, yet it’s paid-in capital is still zero,” the alert said.
“Moreover, over 80 per cent of the projects it took were [residential] communities from...
title: Zero capital, 116 projects: AI spots the devils in the details of China corruption case

author: Phoebe Zhang,William Zheng
description:
Drones are banned, security cameras bristle at intersections and some residents have been asked to vacate their homes as the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen counts down to the Apec meetings.
Thousands of government officials, journalists, tourists and entrepreneurs are expected to descend on the city next week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, where President Xi Jinping will hold talks with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as he chairs the 33rd Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting from...
title: As Apec looms, China’s Shenzhen wraps up preparations for its toughest stress test ever

author: Carol Yang
description:
China and South Korea have agreed to use next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen to advance bilateral ties, according to their top diplomats.
The pledge by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun after talks in Beijing on Friday comes as Seoul seeks Beijing’s help to revive stalled dialogue with Pyongyang.
The Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting from November 18 to 19 is expected to mark the third summit talks between South Korean President...
title: China, South Korea vow to deepen ties at Apec summit as Seoul pushes North Korea talks

author: Shi Huang
description:
From A-list underwear campaigns to everyday wardrobe staples, tight briefs are often hailed as the ultimate symbol of masculine appeal.
However, a major new study out of China suggests that choosing tight underwear over classic boxer shorts could lead to higher rates of erectile dysfunction, premature ejaculation and prostatitis.
A snug fit also impairs sperm quality, according to the findings published in the Asian Journal of Andrology last month.
Loose underwear may offer a simple alternative...
title: Wearing briefs boosts erectile dysfunction risk, 26,000-man study in China finds

author: Xiaojun Wang
description:
China is updating a law that has underpinned one of the most remarkable industrial transformations of our time. After two decades of rapid renewable-energy development, China is preparing to rewrite the rules that have guided, supported and guarded its energy revolution.
The draft revision to China’s Renewable Energy Law was released on November 6 for public comment until December 5.
Twenty years ago, China, having just joined the World Trade Organization, saw energy consumption surge as...
title: China should share its renewable energy expertise

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Nearly a year after taking effect, the landmark High Seas Treaty risks becoming another geopolitical battleground among major powers, observers have warned.
Ratified by 105 countries, including China but not the United States and Russia, the Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) is the most significant maritime pact in decades, governing international waters that cover nearly two-thirds of the global ocean.
While the treaty was designed to safeguard marine ecosystems and...
title: Could major power politics stall the landmark High Seas Treaty?

author: Ling Xin
description:
The world’s first attempt to edit genes inside a child’s brain, which killed a six-year-old girl in Shanghai last year, has led to the firing of scientists following an official investigation that found they had broken research rules and taken money from her family.
The investigation, ordered by the Communist Party’s Shanghai municipal committee and the local government, concluded on Friday that the researchers had not shared worrying results from monkey tests with the girl’s doctors beforehand....
title: Chinese scientists fired after child dies in world’s first brain gene-editing attempt

author: Amber Wang
description:
The Chinese military is mining big data to get better recruits and stamp out corruption in the march towards its centenary next year.
As part of an overhaul called “end-to-end sunshine” recruitment, the People’s Liberation Army has been commanded to use data-driven systems across the the enlistment process to build a military “focused on war readiness”.
The orders came this month from the general offices of the Central Military Commission and State Council and mark a renewed push to eradicate...
title: Cleaner, smarter, big data: the PLA’s bet on ‘sunshine’ military recruitment

author: Alex Lo
description:
“I thought spooks were supposed to be stealthy,” the uncouth, flatulent anti-hero Jackson Lamb complains in the hit British spy series Slow Horses as an annoying underling loudly enters his rundown office building, known to fans as Slough House.
I have no idea if Alice Huang, the alleged love interest of billionaire Jensen Huang – who resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday – is really a Chinese Mata Hari. My own knowledge of espionage is confined to reading John le Carre and Robert Ludlum, and...
title: Don’t take Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s ‘sex’ scandal at face value

author: Holly Chik
description:
China owns 80 per cent of the world’s underwater data centre patents, giving it a decisive lead in critical technologies, according to a two-decade study of global patents in the field.
The findings reveal a shift away from the West in the race to build future green computing infrastructure, as China transforms from an early follower into the dominant force in subsea data technologies.
“China holds competitive edges in engineering-oriented technologies such as modular construction and in situ...
title: China holds 80% of world’s underwater data centre patents as computing energy demands grow

author: Nayan Seth
description:
The White House on Friday confirmed an unprecedented meeting between leaders of the US, China and Russia has been scheduled to take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen next week.
“President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the President of the United States, the President of the People’s Republic of China and the President of the Russian Federation,” said Olivia Wales, the White House assistant press...
title: White House confirms US-China-Russia trilateral on Apec sidelines
